title: ☁️ Alibaba's AI Cloud Revenue Jumps 53% — but Losses Eat the Profits!
body: ☁️ Alibaba's AI Cloud Revenue Jumps 53% — but Losses Eat the Profits!

Alibaba announced that revenue from its AI and cloud computing business jumped 53% in the last quarter, with revenue from external customers growing 64% — a sign of strong demand for computing power and AI applications. The company's total revenue reached about 271.52 billion yuan, up 10% from last year.

But the picture isn't entirely rosy: the adjusted operating losses of the AI labs, including the "Qwen" model business, reached about 10.5 billion yuan, exceeding the profits made by the cloud and computing operations in the same period. The reason is the cost of developing competing models: specialized processors, research teams, data centers, and expensive infrastructure.

Alibaba also faces semiconductor restrictions that complicate its access to some advanced American hardware, so it is investing in developing local processors and improving the efficiency of its "Qwen" models to reduce dependence on imports. The results show that commercial demand for AI in China is strong, but turning it into a sustainable, profitable business requires controlling costs and converting growth into lasting profits.
Simply put: selling AI capabilities is profitable, but building the models themselves is very expensive — and the hard equation is: how do you grow fast without costs eating you alive?
Can Chinese companies compete with America despite the chip restrictions?
